5 unchanged paragraphs, under The old problem {#problem}, What we already have {#have}

**A metermeter, and an account in the reader's browser.**own vault.** This newsroom already charges per use, without a server keeping the balance: every reader starts with £5 of credit, each page draws a few pence from it, the credit is kept in the reader's browser, and the balance can go below zero until they top up with a £5 payment link, live since 11 October. I wrote about why in [paying after the value](../../paying-after-the-value.md). The account is kept in the browser and, when the reader opens their vault with a passkey, carried into it: one file per device, a balance consolidated across devices, and a lane that browsers without the passkey can write to. What is not built is the check: the page a payment returns to adds the credit, and does not verify it. [The reading account, as built](../../the-reading-account-as-built.md) lists every piece.
